source.title: TacGen: Touch Is a Necessary Dimension of Physical-World Representation -- Addressing Tactile Data Scarcity with Scalable Vision-to-Touch Alignment and Generation
source.authors: Wanghao Ye; Aarosh Das; Sihan Chen; Yiting Wang; Bowei Tian; Guoheng Sun; Shwai He; Zheyu Shen; Ziyao Wang; Yexiao He; Zhaoyi Liu; Meng Liu; Yuning Zhang; Meng Feng; Ziyi Wang; Yilong Dai; Yifei Dong; Siyuan Peng; Zhenle Duan; Joshua Liu; Lang Xiong; Ang Li

record.file_problem: The paper text is substantially complete. Some final figure text is garbled, but the reported retrieval results and relevant tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests paired cross-modal representation alignment in a vision–tactile setting, a new modality setting for the claim’s representation-mapping version. It does not test convergence as models scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports physical-property probes, tactile generation, and downstream manipulation outcomes, but these do not measure convergence of representations as model size or capability increases. The alignment-data-size sweep reports downstream probe gains, not model scaling or representation convergence. The paired V↔T retrieval results are the direct evidence relevant to V4; they test correspondence after learned projection heads, not low-loss interchangeability.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own InfoNCE MLP projection heads on paired RGB and DIGIT-tactile features from frozen DINOv2 encoders. The V↔T retrieval numbers are a sanity check on that method; the authors say they confirm the alignment learns cross-modal content. This is the study's own method's performance, not a test of whether independently trained models' representations converge or map onto each other with little loss. It has no model-scale sweep, no comparison of independently trained models on the same data, and no feature-universality analysis. The temperature sweep tunes the study's own training. The main results are probe gains from adding touch, which no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that touch is a necessary physical evidence channel: adding aligned tactile features improves mass, density, hardness and force probes and TACTO manipulation over vision-only. Generated tactile latents recover most of this utility. Paired retrieval is reported only as a check that the alignment learns cross-modal content, not as a claim about representation convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains InfoNCE projection heads on paired RGB and tactile data and evaluates paired retrieval and downstream physical-property probes. It does not compare independently trained model representations as model size or capability changes.
record.method_sensitivity: V→T top-1 retrieval varies across the InfoNCE temperature sweep, from 0.113 ± 0.020 at τ = 0.03 to 0.203 ± 0.010 at τ = 0.20; the paper-default τ = 0.07 gives 0.182 ± 0.012 in the three-seed temperature cohort.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen DINOv2 RGB and DIGIT-tactile features, after InfoNCE-trained MLP heads, give paired V↔T top-1 retrieval of about 0.19 on 459 test pairs (median rank 6–7). A single-seed canonical-budget checkpoint gives 0.017. Retrieval varies with temperature (0.113–0.203).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision and tactile encoder features can be brought into partial correspondence by learned contrastive projection heads trained on paired data.

record.problems: The retrieval results concern RGB–tactile pairs rather than the claim’s vision–language example. Retrieval above chance does not establish that one representation can substitute for another with little loss. The paper reports different retrieval results for canonical-budget and fixed-step training configurations.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for physical-property probes, tactile-generation utility, or manipulation success: those outcomes do not measure the claim’s representational convergence or mapping. No rows for alignment-data-size scaling because it reports downstream probe deltas rather than representation convergence.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep; the data-size sweep varies alignment training data for the study's own heads.
No vision–language models or image–caption pairs.
Alignment seeds are reported only as variance of probe and retrieval scores, not as feature or subspace overlap across initializations.
No linear map, stitching, relative representation or unpaired mapping between independently trained models; only the study's own jointly trained contrastive heads are evaluated.
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits compared across models.
No comparison of similarity measures or OOD inputs for a convergence measure.
No test of alignment plateau or of the causes of convergence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/V4 'tests' call is reclassified as T4. The retrieval rows evaluate the paper's own alignment method and its hyperparameters. The paper also cites visuo-haptic convergence in the brain (Amedi et al.) as motivation only.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep across independently trained models; the alignment-data-size sweep changes training-set size, not model scale.
No vision–language models or paired images and captions are tested; the paired modalities are RGB vision and tactile sensing.
Alignment checkpoints are retrained across seeds, but the paper does not test whether independently initialized networks learn common features or shared subspaces.

Tests learned projection-head alignment and paired retrieval for RGB and tactile features, not low-loss interchangeability, linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are measured.

No comparison of alternative similarity measures or out-of-distribution inputs for convergence. An InfoNCE temperature sweep is reported, but it changes training settings rather than the similarity measure.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain convergence.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Paired RGB–DIGIT tactile features aligned with learned projection heads
reader_labels.reason: Paired retrieval is consistently above chance, but top-1 retrieval is 0.017 for the canonical single-seed reference and 0.188/0.191 for the five-seed fixed-step V→T/T→V results; this is evidence of correspondence, not demonstrated low-loss interchangeability (r1–r3).
